summary: Lakeview Mountain, WA: L-4 cab built 1935 and abandoned 1945; it has since collapsed, debris is reported, and the south side is on Yakama Reservation land where access needs permission.

facts.design: L-4 cab built in 1935; the sources read describe no tower under it
facts.status_note: Cab abandoned in 1945 and has collapsed; one history page says a significant amount of debris remains

access.note: South side lies within the Yakama Reservation; north half is in Goat Rocks Wilderness. The sources read describe no public route to the site; the reservation is listed as administrator.

events.note: Cab abandoned about ten years after it was built

evidence.supports: L-4 cab built in 1935; abandoned since 1945; has since collapsed
evidence.quote: The present L-4 cab, built in 1935, has been abandoned since 1945 and has since collapsed.

evidence.quote: For many years, the lookout sat alone, rotting away and finally it collapsed.

evidence.quote: The North half of Lakeview Mountain is in the Goat Rocks Wilderness, while the South side is inside the Yakama Nation.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register says Yakima Indian Reservation; firelookout.com says Yakama Indian Reservation and Willhite says Yakama Nation. The spelling differs; the pages treat them as the same reservation.

notes_for_editor: History (1935 build, 1945 abandonment, collapse) agrees across all four pages. Present condition rests on undated pages; the debris statement comes from one page only. Access is permission-only in the record; a web search found no published tribal permit process, and it found no public access route, so the tribe's land or natural resources office is the contact to verify with. Wilderness-side (north half) rules were not read. No staffing dates or fires were found in the sources read. No photos added.
